docs.title: Wah-Lah ProPulse AI
docs.text: ProPulse is a background, event-driven agent orchestrator. Applications submit signals; ProPulse evaluates triggers and policy, queues work, and returns an outcome without requiring a dashboard.

docs.title: Start locally
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env
make up
make demo

The default local profile uses MongoDB, Redis, and zero-cost adapter defaults. See the quickstart and operations runbook.

docs.title: Project map
docs.text:
• packages/propulse-core: protocol, state machine, signing, entitlement and bus abstractions.
  • apps/api: FastAPI gateway and versioned endpoints.
  • apps/worker: orchestration, agent execution, voice coalescing, and guarded webhook delivery.
  • apps/scheduler: scheduled work and lease recovery.
  • packages/sdk-android, packages/sdk-js, packages/sdk-python: client SDKs.

docs.title: Important status note
docs.text: Local automated tests and SDK checks should be run before each release. Production deployment, signing/publishing credentials, and public service DNS are environment-specific and are not supplied by this source repository.

docs.title: AGPL compliance
docs.text: The server-side project is licensed under AGPL-3.0-or-later. SDK packages are licensed separately under Apache-2.0 as described in the repository license files. Commercial licensing terms are documented in LICENSE.commercial; review them with qualified counsel before relying on them.

docs.title: Source disclosure
docs.text: The API exposes GET /source for source-repository and license metadata. The response must reflect the repository URL and exact build commit for the deployed artifact.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
• Include the applicable license and copyright notices.
  • Preserve source availability obligations for modified network-accessible AGPL software.
  • Keep third-party dependency notices and SBOM artifacts with releases.
  • Verify that SDK licensing boundaries match the contents actually distributed.
  • Do not describe a release as compliant solely because a license file exists; verify distribution and deployment practices too.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. /v1 is stable. Breaking changes require a new major path.
  2. Additive changes ship freely: new optional params, new response fields, new routes.
  3. Minimum deprecation window: 12 months for /v1, 6 months for SDK majors.

docs.title: Wire protocol negotiation
docs.text: SDKs send X-PP-Protocol: <n>. The server supports current through current-2 and echoes the negotiated version in X-PP-Protocol on every response. Unknown higher versions are downgraded, never rejected — this is what keeps 3-year-old installs working.

docs.title: Deprecation signalling
docs.text: RFC 8594 headers on deprecated routes:

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• Core library: protocol envelope, state machine, key and HMAC helpers, rate limiting, entitlement logic, licensing checks, and adapters.
  • API gateway: FastAPI routes for health, device registration, pulse operations, keys, billing, licensing, and source disclosure.
  • Worker: consumes work from the configured bus, evaluates agent budgets, coalesces voice output, and sends outbound webhooks through SSRF guards.
  • Scheduler: coordinates scheduled ticks and reaps orphaned leases.
  • Storage and bus: MongoDB for durable application state and Redis Streams for distributed work; an in-memory bus is available for tests/local use.
  • SDKs: Android, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Python clients sign requests using the protocol defined by the core package.

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
1. A client sends a signed signal to the API.
  2. Middleware validates request timing, nonce, protocol version, idempotency, and tenant limits.
  3. The API persists the request and publishes work.
  4. Workers evaluate policy and produce an outcome.
  5. A client acknowledges delivery or polls for the next action.

docs.title: Security boundaries
docs.text: Request authentication, nonce freshness, idempotency, rate limits, webhook egress controls, and licensing checks are enforced in server code. See the threat model. Production secret management, network policy, and operational access controls must still be configured for the target environment.

docs.title: What is being sold
docs.text:
A complete, revenue-generating SaaS with zero founder dependency.

Server 100 % AGPL-3.0, self-hostable, no proprietary runtime SDKs Apache-2.0, three platforms, wire-compatible Commercial layer Stripe subscriptions and $15k/$25k buy-outs, fully automated Infrastructure docker compose up on any $6 VPS. No managed services required Bus factor 1 for code review, 0 for operation

docs.title: Why there is no founder in the loop
docs.text: Function Automation Signup API key minted via POST /v1/keys; no form Onboarding README + make up + two-line SDK Payment Headless Stripe Checkout; webhook upgrades the key in Mongo Tier enforcement EntitlementService reads a versioned, invalidatable cache Upgrade prompt 429 body field and X-PP-Upgrade-Url header Overage billing Local usage_ledger → Stripe Meters Enterprise close /v1/license/tiers + /v1/license/quote + Stripe one-time Agreement Generated from template on payment, stored on the license document Private repo access GitHub App invite; status: pending flag for follow-up Support SUPPORT.md SLAs; no live chat required Ops Runbook covers every P1 with copy-pasteable commands

docs.title: Revenue model
docs.text:
1. Subscriptions — Free 1 000/mo → Pro $19 → Team $99 → metered overage.
  2. Commercial buy-out — $15k (single product) / $25k (unlimited + OEM). Perpetual.
  3. Renewals — $3k / $5k annually for continued updates.
  4. Marketplace — 30 % take on third-party trigger packs (post-1.0).
  5. Enterprise self-host license — for AGPL-averse buyers.

docs.title: Unit economics
docs.text:
• Marginal cost per 1 000 pulses: ≈ $0 (Redis Streams, one Mongo write, on-device TTS).
  • Cloud TTS is the only variable cost, and only on Pro+ with server TTS enabled.
  • Infra floor: one 2 vCPU / 4 GB VPS serves ≈ 2 000 rps of /signal.
  • Gross margin at Pro: > 95 %. At Team: > 98 %.

docs.title: Tech moat
docs.text:
• At-least-once delivery with a proven no-duplicate invariant, chaos-tested nightly.
  • Deterministic replay of agent runs from recorded tool I/O.
  • Battery governor with a measured < 1 %/hr idle budget.
  • Coalescing engine — the perceived-quality differentiator competitors will clone.
  • AGPL boundary that converts enterprise forks into invoices.

docs.title: Due-diligence answers, pre-written
docs.text:
• Is anything licensed non-commercially? No. AGPL + Apache-2.0 + our own commercial terms.
  • Can it run without AWS? Yes. Any Docker host. BUS_DRIVER=memory for a single box.
  • Single point of failure in code? No. All state is in Mongo/Redis; every service is stateless.
  • What breaks if the founder disappears? Nothing in production. GOVERNANCE.md names successors.
  • What is the transferable IP? The engine, the SDKs, the trigger taxonomy, the brand.
  • What needs a human on day 1 of ownership? Merging PRs. That is the entire list.
  • Recurring infra cost? One VPS. Mongo and Redis are self-hosted containers.

docs.title: Post-acquisition 90-day plan
docs.text: Week Action 1 Rotate SECRET_KEY, Stripe keys, LICENSE_SIGNING_SECRET; transfer DNS 2 Re-run the restore drill; confirm backups land somewhere you own 3 Turn on the marketplace waitlist; publish three first-party trigger packs 4 Raise Pro to $29 with a grandfathered cohort; measure churn 6 Launch the iOS SDK from the same wire protocol 8 Add a self-serve annual plan (2 months free) to lift LTV 12 Open the marketplace at 70/30 and onboard five tool authors

docs.title: Known growth levers, ranked
docs.text:
1. Trigger pack library (e-commerce, fitness, fintech) — pure margin.
  2. iOS + Web SDKs — 3× addressable market, same protocol.
  3. Managed cloud tier — the only thing people actually want to buy.
  4. Marketplace revenue share — compounding supply-side lock-in.
  5. Compliance add-ons — SOC 2 report, DPA, EU residency, audit export.

docs.title: Deprecation policy
docs.text: Surface Minimum notice Announced via /v1 route 12 months Deprecation + Sunset headers, CHANGELOG, docs Response field 12 months docs + OpenAPI deprecated: true SDK major 6 months SDK CHANGELOG, in-app warning, release notes Wire protocol version 24 months X-PP-Protocol negotiation + docs Driver / adapter 6 months startup warning log

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
1. Mark deprecated in code and OpenAPI.
  2. Emit headers. Log a counter per deprecated route.
  3. Announce in CHANGELOG under Deprecations.
  4. After the window, remove in the next major.
  5. Never remove in a patch or minor.

docs.title: ProPulse licensing notes
docs.text:
• Server and core engine: AGPL-3.0-or-later.
  • Android, JavaScript, and Python SDKs: Apache-2.0.
  • A future commercial propulse-pro package, if distributed, has a separate commercial license.

The AGPL license text is in LICENSES/AGPL-3.0-or-later.txt; the SDK license text is in LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt. See TRADEMARK.md for the separate treatment of project names and marks.

The GET /source endpoint is intended to help deployments provide source and build information. It does not replace the license obligations that apply to a specific distribution or deployment. Obtain qualified legal advice for questions about a particular use or commercial arrangement.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Docker Engine with the Compose plugin
  • Git
  • Python 3.12 and uv for local development
  • Node.js 18+ for the JavaScript SDK

docs.title: Start the local stack
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env
make up
make doctor
make demo

The .env.example file documents supported defaults. Keep real credentials in a local, untracked .env file or a secret manager; never commit them.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
make test
make lint
cd packages/sdk-js
npm ci
npm test
npm run build
npm run lint

The local demonstration validates the configured local path; it does not establish production readiness, external billing setup, DNS, or deployment credentials.

docs.title: Local lifecycle
docs.text:
make doctor
make up
make logs
make demo
make test
make down

Use make down to stop the local stack. Avoid destructive targets such as make nuke unless removing local data is intended.

docs.title: Health and troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Check make doctor first for environment and dependency checks.
  • Use make logs to inspect service logs.
  • Confirm the configured MongoDB and Redis URLs in the local environment.
  • Confirm adapter settings; the local default adapters are intended for development and demonstration.
  • If a service does not become healthy, inspect its own logs before restarting the whole stack.

docs.title: Production incident response
docs.text: Do not use the local demo checklist as a production incident procedure. Production deployment, backups, key rotation, alert routing, rollback, and access controls must be configured and tested for the selected hosting environment before launch.

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text: The repository includes Prometheus alert rules, an OpenTelemetry collector configuration, and a k6 smoke workload under infra/.

docs.title: Local inspection
docs.text:
• Review infra/prometheus/alerts.yml for alert conditions.
  • Review infra/otel/collector.yaml for configured telemetry receivers and exporters.
  • Review infra/k6/smoke.js before running load tests against any target.

Telemetry collection and alert delivery depend on the runtime configuration and endpoints supplied by the operator. Do not send production traffic to a local or staging stack without explicit authorization and capacity checks.

docs.title: Assets
docs.text: API keys, tenant data, notification content, billing state, commercial license keys.

docs.title: Boundaries & threats
docs.text: Boundary Threat Control Device → Edge Key extraction from APK Public keys are scoped, cert-pinned, HMAC-signed, per-device limited Device → Edge Replay 300 s timestamp window + Redis SETNX nonce Edge → Gateway Header spoofing Private network; X-PP-* stripped and re-derived at the edge Gateway → Bus Message forgery Private Redis; envelopes carry tenant + trace Worker → Webhook SSRF DNS resolve → IP allowlist; no redirects by default Agent → Tools Prompt injection Tool args validated against JSON Schema; results never treated as instructions Stripe → Gateway Forged webhook stripe-signature verify + stripe_events unique index Operator Secret sprawl OIDC in CI, no long-lived cloud creds, Docker secrets in prod

docs.title: Assumptions we state openly
docs.text:
• Public API keys are extractable. Defence is scoping + signing + pinning, not secrecy.
  • Redis loss is a degradation, not an outage (rate limiting fails open).
  • A malicious tenant cannot starve others: rate limiting is per-tenant as well as per-key.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Your reverse proxy config, your own app's auth, DoS at the network edge before TLS.

docs.title: SLSA
docs.text: Level 2. Builds run on GitHub-hosted runners with provenance attestation and keyless cosign signatures. Base images pinned by digest. Actions pinned to commit SHAs.

docs.title: Architecture decision records
docs.text:
These records capture the major design choices for the ProPulse platform.

  • 0001 — Record decisions
  • 0002 — Redis Streams over Kafka
  • 0003 — License boundary
  • 0004 — Key format and hashing
  • 0005 — No billing dashboard
  • 0006 — Headless AGPL enforcement

docs.title: ADR 0001: Record decisions as architecture decision records
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ProPulse combines a server, workers, scheduler, mobile SDKs, billing boundaries, and deployment automation. Unrecorded design changes make the implementation difficult to audit and can create incompatible assumptions across components.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Record decisions that affect architecture, security, licensing, compatibility, cost, or operations in numbered files under docs/adr/. Accepted records are immutable; later changes supersede them with a new ADR. Implementation and release changes should reference the relevant ADR.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The rationale and reversal cost remain reviewable. Contributors must add an ADR when a change breaks the SDK integration promise, changes API compatibility, crosses a license boundary, or introduces always-on infrastructure. Small implementation details do not require an ADR.

docs.title: 2. Redis Streams as the default event bus
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23
  • Deciders: steering

docs.title: Context
docs.text: We need at-least-once delivery, consumer groups, replay, and dead-lettering. The constraint that dominates: docker compose up must boot a working stack with zero external services. Kafka means KRaft or Zookeeper, a JVM, and 2 GB of RAM before the product does anything.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Redis Streams is the default. A Bus protocol with a memory adapter keeps tests instant and single-box deploys trivial.

Delivery guarantees come from XREADGROUP, XAUTOCLAIM, XACK, XADD with approximate MAXLEN, and idempotent handlers keyed on dedupe_key.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Boot time under 30 s, RAM floor ~400 MB.
  • At-least-once with reclaim-based crash recovery.
  • Ceiling around a few hundred thousand events/minute on one Redis — enough for the first several thousand tenants.
  • NATS/Kafka/SQS remain a future adapter, not a rewrite.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• Kafka: best throughput and retention, worst local ergonomics.
  • NATS JetStream: great fit, another binary, less familiar to Python devs.
  • Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY: adds a database dependency and weaker replay.
  • SQS: managed cost, not offline.

docs.title: Reversal cost
docs.text: Medium. The Bus protocol is narrow (publish/consume/ack/reclaim/dlq), so an adapter is a few hundred lines — not a rearchitecture.

docs.title: ADR 0003: Keep the open-core license boundary explicit
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ProPulse offers an AGPL server and separately licensed SDKs. The repository must make the license of each component visible and prevent SDK packages from depending on server implementation details.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: The server and core engine use AGPL-3.0-or-later. The Android, JavaScript, and Python SDKs use Apache-2.0. Any future closed-source propulse-pro package is distributed separately under a commercial license and may depend on the core only through a narrow published interface. Automated boundary checks run in CI.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Every shipped component must have an explicit SPDX license declaration and corresponding license text. Dependencies and imports crossing component boundaries require review. The commercial license does not grant rights to the Wah-Lah or ProPulse trademarks.

docs.title: ADR 0004: Use distinct public and secret API-key formats
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Public client keys may be embedded in application packages and must be verifiable on every request. Secret keys must remain server-side and should be resistant to offline guessing if a credential store is exposed.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use visibly distinct pp_pub_ and pp_sec_ prefixes. Store public-key digests with SHA-256 for fast verification; store secret-key verifiers with Argon2id. Scope each key by allowed capabilities, never log plaintext keys, and use request HMAC signatures with timestamp and nonce validation for replay resistance. Public keys are not treated as confidential credentials.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Key rotation, scope ceilings, rate limits, and request signing remain part of the security model. Any key-format change requires a compatibility plan and tests for malformed, tampered, and wrong-secret cases.

docs.title: 5. Headless billing — no dashboard
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A billing dashboard is a second product: auth, sessions, SSR, styling, a support surface. Every hour on it is an hour not spent on the engine.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Stripe Checkout and the Stripe Customer Portal do the UI. Our surface is four endpoints:

  • GET /v1/billing/plans — public catalogue
  • POST /v1/billing/checkout — returns a URL
  • POST /v1/billing/portal — returns a URL
  • POST /v1/billing/webhook — upgrades the key

The upgrade prompt is a 429 carrying upgrade_url in the body and X-PP-Upgrade-Url in the headers.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Zero frontend to maintain. Stripe owns PCI, tax, 3DS, invoices, dunning.
  • Conversion happens inside the developer's own CLI or app — no context switch.
  • BILLING_DRIVER=null means a full product with no Stripe account at all.
  • A marketing site is optional, not load-bearing.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• Custom dashboard: control, cost, time.
  • Stripe Pricing Table embed: still a page, less control over the funnel.
  • Paddle / LemonSqueezy: viable merchant-of-record; Stripe's API is better and the BillingAdapter protocol lets us swap.

docs.title: Reversal cost
docs.text: Low. A dashboard can be added later without touching the engine.

docs.title: 6. Headless AGPL enforcement via /source
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Open-core fails in one of two ways: nobody adopts it, or everybody adopts it and nobody pays. The second is a distribution problem, not a legal one. Enterprise legal teams reject AGPL by reflex, and most never read section 13.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Make compliance a ten-second curl, and make the alternative a ten-second purchase.

  • GET /source returns repo, license, exact commit SHA, archive URL, and a plain-English notices block stating what you must and must not do.
  • GET /v1/license/tiers returns the two buy-outs with prices and grants.
  • POST /v1/license/checkout takes payment and auto-issues a perpetual, offline-verifiable key plus a generated agreement.
  • docs/agpl-compliance.md leads with "you do not have to open-source your app."

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The legal objection becomes a one-line verification a developer can run.
  • Every self-hosted deployment carries a permanent, visible upsell in its own API.
  • LICENSE.commercial exists before the first inbound email, so deals close in days.
  • Requires a CLA so we can dual-license contributions.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• MIT core with a paid Pro module: weaker pull toward paying.
  • BSL with a 4-year conversion: not OSI-approved, confusing to procurement.
  • No commercial option: forks keep mods private, we never invoice.

docs.title: Reversal cost
docs.text: High. Loosening core to permissive forfeits the buy-out funnel permanently.
